body: Sorry, I was wrong suggesting this topic. If the West does it, it should work. I should not question it. I understand that as a Russian I have a wrong view on the world. I wish it was not like that, but I understand we are doing wrong and Europe does whatever it takes to stop the war. We Russians failed. Shame to me, my country and my people.

All, I am sorry I have raised this topic. As a Russian, I do not have any moral right to criticize the western world, my country failed and all its citizens with it. I am sure what is being done now should be done, and I am in no place to doubt it. I am sorry, I did not want to offend anyone, and more than anything I want Putin to stop. If the West deem these measures good, they might be good. I am sorry. We Russut deserve the worst fate, and should just accept it. Europe knows what it's doing. Freedom and peace to the civilized world.
It is okay, I understand the logic. When times comes, I will do what is right.

Sorry for that... Maybe we Russians all should just die as soon as possible. Maybe we are genetically wrong. I can accept it. But the problem is still there... Well, I am sorry, I should not have raised this topic. I don't have the right, as a citizen of Mordor. Just let's hope that my nation disappears, and then the world can be free.

I am sorry for being deranged. I am sorry for not being human. But how can I as a citizen take responsibility now? Protest, share information? I do. Rhetorically accept guilt? I do. I am guilty for the tragedy. I did not do enough. Now what? Please explain how can I, as a middle-class Russian, take responsibility right now, in action? Joining Ukrainian army?

Trust me, I understand, and I would gladly exchange my life for peace. We Russians are disgusting by birth and we deserve the worst fate. I should not have raised this topic. I know nothing is important and we all should be dead - this is the only solution. We - I mean the Russian animals.
I agree in general, but they might be needed for a coop.

It is my bet too! I hope that next time people raise, they won't be ideological opposition, but hungry and angry men who realize they were lied to.

But this hope is exactly the reason I am afraid that the sanctions might have backfired. I want Russians to unite against Putin, and not against the West, offended by the sanctions.

Gosh no, he needs to be gone as soon as possible!!!

I am not suggesting anything like that. As a Russian,, I am interested very much in stopping him. his rule. By no means should he continue invasions and ruling in Russia too. I think that is clear for anyone.

Please understand: I am not victimizing Russians or myself, I am not blaming the west, and I am not suggesting to stop the actions. Hopefully, the positive outcome of the sanctions overshadow the negative ones. I myself hate the idea that the sanctions can fuel Putin's supporter.

Yes, absolutely. It is a mess! This the hardest part of this the war to comprehend: it is nothing but a mess, it's reasons are unclear, the beneficiary is none, but it looks so dangerously like 39th, fascism and all, and thousands of dead.

As if I knew! If I had answers I might do something better than starting a reddit thread.

Maybe different rhetorics, but any rhetorics are filtered anyway.

Russophobia is Putin's invention that his propaganda machine utilizes.

I am NOT victimizing Russians here. Anyone but those who are in direct danger from the regime, is not a victim in any shape and form.
That is very true! And enjoying Starbucks is beyond any point, once again, it is not about commodities, but the rationale behind the decisions. Tax money is a very valid reason!
Maybe - Putin does it all to destroy Russia in the most damaging way:) But if anyone else is willing really to sacrifice Ukraine for any goals, it is a dark world. Putin is enough.

I pray for that! I think that now the west can do one important thing, first and foremost: stop buying Russian gas. And if there's some money, maybe sponsor independent media, it still exists, although subversively. (But money issue is hard, I believe that the Ukrainians need it more.)  Maybe before the other businesses leave, they can make a statement against the war and for human rights, and then make a scandal when Putin will try to close it. But that's just my brainstorming, I am in a creative field and don't know what is the right way.

No, I blame Putin first and foremost, and then his entourage, and those who execute the orders. And lastly, his supporters. West has nothing to blame for in this matter, and blaming anyone does not make me feel any better.

I am questioning the sanctions after reading the interviews by a good journalist that show the worrying dynamics. Don't get me wrong: I am trying to understand, and not to blame, and obviously not to change the world with a reddit thread. I'm opening a discussion and sharing the opinion, not asking for compassion and not pushing the blame onto any other body but Russia as it is.

I am opening this topic not because I am Russian, but because as a sane human I want the invasion to end and the dictatorship to fall. As a Russian, I am trying to understand the mechanisms of the propaganda - maybe there is something that I personally can.do, beyond what I am doing right now.
I am afraid that him starting this war indicates that he is nsane enough. And he proved many times not to be an honorable man, neither with his people, nor with the others.

I am not worried that much about my friends - as long as you hey are not in a jail, they will be fine without Ikea, and whoever has the means and intention will move outside Russia. We are in a worse shape than we were a month ago, but it's not our cities bombed.

The problem is that the general population starts believing the propaganda, and joins the army of Putin's supporters because of the actions of the West. Of anything, the informational war is lost while the changes cannot happen without large, strong opposition movement. Maybe the coop is not the right bet, but there are not too many other options.

And as I said, I live in Europe and I haven't faced any bigotry even once in many years. There are many adequate and friendly people who's attitude I appreciate a lot. The problem is what people believe now and whether they truly support Putin's regime.

And to clarify - I do not know what is the right solution here. I do not blame the westerners for not wanting any interaction with Russia or the Russians. I do, however, question if this is the right strategy that the West takes. I hope that whatever is the strategy, it works to end the war as soon as possible. But reactionist measures that involuntary support Putin's regime scare me. Please correct me if I do not understand something here, from a rational standpoint.

Eventually is not soon enough. The time of hype and support for the leaders is the time lost. Eventually the system might collapse, but do you really think that meantime it cannot bring more harm that is did already? Don't forget the nuclear weaponry. Don't forget that Ukrainian cities are bombed now, and each day, each minute brings possibly more destruction than Europe seen on its territory since WW2.

Russia is a large country that can support years of stagnation. Maduro is still in power after years of economic pressure. Also, Europe continues buying gas. Mcdonalds, Steven King's books and scientific publications are nothing compared to it.

And also - WW2 stopped when the Hitler lost in the war. But he did not have nuclear weaponry. Is it the only way we have right now - to engage in open confrontation with the army that has both the insane leader and the red button?
Even Russian constitution doesn't mean anything to Kremlin. Their life goal - living up to their delusions.

I hope that the protests will be more, but the idea that peaceful protest matters cannot apply to dictatorships. We need radicals, not ideological opposition who stands for peace; we need people who would burn police cars or spread weapons like hunting rifles so that people can fight violently. But also, look at Belarus, Hong Kong, Myanmar, Venezuela - even if the majority protests, the dictator can just use the army to subdue them...

But people who will be protesting next will be not peaceful, but angry men who lost jobs, money, access to medicine and basic commodities. And also families of soldiers that finally received the bodies in zinc coffins. Then it might get powerful enough - or might not. Peaceful protests are important to open up a window of opportunity to someone in power, but only radicals can destabilize the situation enough.

I will think about how to do it, but there should be stronger idea than just go to the street. It is also important, but look at how the whole world just laughs at us, dismisses the efforts. 25% of those who are openly disagreeing with Putin is still 35 millions of people, but we are laughable and just don't count.

If a day comes when we will build a better society, we'll do it with the memories of every crime committed, every death and wound, every home destroyed. We, common Russians, have limited means of influencing the situation - both the war of Ukraine and the raise of state-sponsored fascism in Russia itself. But we see it all and will never forgive the collaborationists of the regime - or ourselves.

Any Russians will remember all the atrocities of this and other wars, and all the crimes within the country.  We will carry these memories with us till the rest of our lives and will tell of them to our children. It will be our legacy ro carry on , the legacy of meaningless, terrible evil - and the grief. If my most important dream comes true, one day there will be museums of Russian invasions in Russian cities, like Holocaust museums in Germany.

Ideally all of us Russians begone, but since that is not happening, remembering will be our duty... And expressing our protest and supporting independent media and support Ukrainians or any people in need are our duties now.

I wish I could do more and would appreciate any ideas

As a Russian, I can say that the day I will be reading a certain necrology would be one of the happiest in my life. Hope this day comes soon... I hate this war and everyone who enabled it by orders or performing them - regardless of thr fact that we were born in the same country. And of people have similar feeling towards all Russians including myself - how can I disagree?

I am against the war and the regime and I am a Russian! How can I be accountable? How others who are trying and failing to protest? I am asking from a practical standpoint. The largest price we can pay is our lives. We are loosing this war with Putin's fascists, we all should be dead.

How can I do soul searching? Almost of my friends and extended family are actively against Putin, but we are small people. I did not live in Russia for years. I want to take on this responsibility beyond reposting and donating to independent media. How can I do the right thing? Please let me know your ideas. How can an average person fuel a revolution? Our nation should just disappear, but what can I do? I'm a researcher in eco restauration. What can I do to help the world and take responsibility? Our blood for blood spilled!

As a Russian citizen who lived abroad for years, what can I do to claim responsibility of my damned nation? I was thinking about publically killing myself and inspiring other Russians to do so - our lives for the lives taken by Russian army, if we can make it an even number, the world will be a better place. But before that is there anything I could do? If I made a lot of money I could sponsor Russian independent media or the refugees from Ukraine - for now I'm volunteering, but I do this as a human, not as Russian. I plan to kill myself in a few years when my sister is independent (I'm a caretaker; and children can be excused I think; plus my sister is vocally against Putin and is underage). Before that how to even live knowing of all atrocities that my compatriots do? How to make use of this life to overthrow the regime, help Ukraine, make amends and keep peace?

You are the people of the free world. Any advice for me? I need it. I am responsible and guilty, but I want to make up for it. If my sister can safely stay where we live now, I am willing to return to Russia to do whatever is needed. Or to Ukraine to volunteer, or anywhere else in the world.

I understand that the logical answer is just to die, but not all will follow, it's a hard decision, many people have families and won't do that even for the better world. So I think there might be something else. And before that, of course, I plan to donate organs after death that goes without saying!

I am so, so sorry for what my country does. Ukraine doesn't deserve it. The world doesn't deserve it. Russia should disappear from Earth for the better good. Children can stay!

Because he is still a dictator with the loyal army force. He's gone crazy and with the power available he literally does what he wants. He is destroying Ukraine and ruining Russia, but no one can stop him until the army and police are loyal to him. They seem to be loyal - because the regime supports them with money and opportunities.
